**Safety parts we’ll add for the “profile photo upload” feature** | Feature | What we’ll put in place | |---------|------------------------| | **Photo or file uploads** | • A private Supabase Storage bucket called `profile-photos`.
• Bucket rules so each logged‑in user can only add, replace or delete *their own* file.
• File‑type and size limits – we’ll default to PNG/JPG only, max 5 MB.
• A “report” button on the image view so a user can flag any inappropriate photo (optional in V1). | --- ## One‑screen plan ``` What we are building: Profile photo upload for logged‑in users. Who uses it: Everyone who signs in (customizable, but we’ll assume “public users” for now). Risk level: Amber – we’re handling personal files and user‑specific data. Day‑one features: 1. User sees “Upload photo” button on their profile page. 2. User can choose a PNG/JPG file smaller than 5 MB. 3. The file is stored in a private bucket; only the uploader can view it. 4. The profile page shows the uploaded photo; if no photo, a default placeholder. 5. (Optional: a “Report photo” link that opens a tiny form). Information it stores: Each user’s photo URL in the Supabase `profiles` table (or a new `profile_photos` table). Personal data; each person only sees their own photo. Logins: yes – uses Supabase Auth (assumes you already have it set up). Each user has an authenticated session. Money: no payments or paid APIs. Built with: Supabase Storage + Supabase Auth in a Lovable app. Steps: 1. Create a private bucket `profile-photos` in Supabase Storage. 2. Add a row‑level‑security (RLS) policy that allows `authenticated` users to `upload`, `list`, `read`, and `delete` only their own folders (`user_id/`). 3. In your Lovable UI, add an “Upload photo” button that opens the browser file picker. 4. On selection, use the Supabase client to upload to `profile-photos/user_id/` with the file name `profile.{ext}`. 5. Store the public URL (or the bucket key) in the `profiles` table next to the user. 6. Show that URL in the profile component; if nil, show a placeholder. 7. (Optional) Add a tiny “Report photo” modal that submits a record to a `photo_reports` table. Safety: key secrets in `.env` (Supabase URL and anon key) hidden, RLS only for the bucket, file‑type/size restriction, single upload per user, confirmation before delete. Not in V1: Multiple photos per user, external CDN, advanced moderation, photo compression, dark‑mode UI, etc. ``` **Does this look right?** Reply **yes** or tell me what you’d like to change. If you’re unsure what “Supabase bucket rules” look like, I can walk you through those next.
